title: PbfuzzCampaign
description: `pbfuzz.campaign.yaml` — the TARGET-PROJECT facts one pbfuzz run needs, and nothing else. pbfuzz's own behaviour lives in pbfuzz-settings.schema.json, and how a fact was decided is shown once in the confirmation panel rather than stored here: an earlier version carried a `provenance` map plus the same evidence again as inline comments, which made a single-file target's campaign 12.8 KB of which ~80% was the same 22 sentences twice. Every field below is read by the engine, the analysis provider or the guards; a field that only described the campaign to a human reader is gone.

version.description: Campaign schema version. Bumped only on a breaking change.

id.description: Campaign identifier; names the state directory `<output.dir>` default and the kanalyzer cache namespace.

confirmed.description: Set by `pbfuzz_campaign confirm` when the user approves the plan-review panel, which also opens PLAN. A hand-written headless campaign must set it explicitly.

repo.description: Absolute path to the target project checkout.

language.description: Drives tracer selection and which analysis providers can apply. `other` is supported: the engine only needs `entry.run_cmd` plus the oracle.

bug.description: What we are trying to trigger, and where.

targets.description: Target locations. Each must resolve to a line carrying an instruction — KAMain silently finds nothing otherwise.

condition.description: The predicate that must hold at this location for the bug to trigger, in source syntax where possible. Carried into PLAN's bug predicates.

build.description: How to build the target: the user's build command, or a script the agent wrote. `pbfuzz_campaign draft` runs it (making a script executable first) and reports what happened; static analysis reuses it for its own bitcode build.

cmd.description: Build command, or the path of a build script.

dir.description: Where to run it. Defaults to `target.repo`.

entry.description: How one input is fed to the program under test. This is the whole of what the engine needs to execute, and the reason the framework is language-agnostic: libFuzzer, Atheris and Jazzer harnesses all run one input from one file, so `run_cmd` with `@@` covers all of them.

kind.description: `api` = the project's existing fuzz harness is used; `executable` = a binary is run end to end.

run_cmd.description: Full command template. `@@` is replaced by the input file path when `input_channel` is `file`; with `stdin` the input is piped and `@@` must not appear.

env.description: Extra environment for the target process, merged over the engine's own.

oracle.description: How a run is judged. Both signals are stderr regexes, which keeps the oracle independent of language and harness.

mode.description: `canary` = pbfuzz inserted its own reach/trigger canaries; `preexisting` = the project already emits usable markers (e.g. Magma's MAGMA_LOG).

reached_pattern.description: Regex matched against stderr to detect that the target location was reached.

triggered_pattern.description: Regex matched against stderr to detect that the bug predicate held.

canary_on_trigger.description: What an inserted trigger canary does. `log` keeps the run alive so one execution can report several signals. Only meaningful with `mode: canary`; omitted when it is the default.

canary_patch.description: Path to the reversible patch holding the inserted canaries, so the target can be restored exactly.

tracer.description: Breakpoint tracer for stage-1 concrete runs. Absent means `tools.tracer` from settings; `auto` picks by `target.language`. Written only when this campaign overrides the setting.

analysis.description: Per-campaign configuration for each auxiliary analysis tool enabled in settings. A tool that could not be made to work is recorded here as disabled with a reason, which is what lets the run continue instead of degrading silently.

static.description: Static analysis inputs, all optional: the analyzer builds its own bitcode the first time it is queried. Whether it runs at all is a setting; `enabled: false` with a `disabled_reason` turns it off for this campaign.

program.description: The link output being analysed (basename of the binary).

bitcode.description: An existing `*.0.0.preopt.bc` to reuse instead of building one.

entries.description: KAMain `-entry-list`. Inferred with llvm-nm: `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` when present, else `main`.

lto_libs.description: Static dependency libraries that must also be LTO-built, or KAMain sees an incomplete call graph.

prebuilt_dir.description: Existing KAMain text outputs to import instead of running the analysis (the Magma SKIP_STATIC_ANALYSIS path).

disabled_reason.description: e.g. `no seeds supplied` — corpus analysis turns itself off rather than failing the run.

mode.description: `critical_bb` needs static analysis; without it the detector degrades to `target_only`.

dir.description: Where state, testcases, logs and the PoC are written. Defaults to the directory containing this campaign file.
